title: Allen Says US Needs Stronger Export-Control Enforcement
title_cn: Allen Says US Needs Stronger Export-Control Enforcement
summary: Michael Allen, Managing Director of Beacon Global Strategies and former special assistant to President George W. Bush in the National Security sector, thinks Congress needs to direct its questions to the Commerce Department and, by extension, the National Security Council process staff about what happened with export-control regulations and what may have held them up. Allen says stronger export controls and beefing up the Department of Commerce are important, including greater enforcement, oversight and investigations. Allen says Trump should make clear to President Xi Jinping that China’s activity involving smuggling and restricted technology could lead Congress to take further action. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was ousted from his post after reports of two affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China. Huang, one of the three engineers who founded the chipmaker in 1993, had been under intense pressure since Sunday, when he admitted to a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singapore-based data center firm Megaspeed International. The Nvidia turmoil rippled through the entire artificial intelligence sector on Thursday, dragging down shares of semiconductor companies.

Emily Chang, Host & Executive Producer of Bloomberg’s ‘The Circuit’
